questions.questionText: Which of the following best explains why binary search runs in O(log N) time?
options: Because it uses a linear scan of the array
Because it examines every element in the array once
Because it sorts the array before searching
Because each recursive call halves the search interval, resulting in log N levels of recursion
questions.correctAnswer: Because each recursive call halves the search interval, resulting in log N levels of recursion
questions.explanation: Binary search repeatedly halves the search interval, so the number of recursive calls (or iterations) is proportional to log N, giving O(log N) time complexity.

questions.questionText: If the array used in the binary‑search step for finding the median were not sorted (i.e., A[i‑1] < A[i] does not hold), what is the most likely effect on the algorithm?
options: The algorithm will still correctly find the median because binary‑search does not depend on ordering
The partition condition A[i‑1] ≤ B[j] and B[j‑1] ≤ A[i] can never be satisfied, causing the search to fail
The algorithm will enter an infinite loop because the mid index never changes
The binary‑search may discard the half containing the correct median, leading to an incorrect result
questions.correctAnswer: The binary‑search may discard the half containing the correct median, leading to an incorrect result
questions.explanation: Binary search relies on the sorted order (A[i‑1] < A[i]) to decide which half of the array can be safely ignored. If the array is unsorted, the comparison used to move left or right is unreliable, so the algorithm may discard the segment that actually contains the median, producing a wrong answer.

questions.questionText: Given the array [12, 7, 9, 20], after sorting it in ascending order, what is the middle value according to the rule that when the array length is even the middle value is the mean of the two middle numbers?
questions.explanation: Sorting the array yields [7, 9, 12, 20]. The two middle numbers are 9 and 12. Their mean is (9+12)/2 = 21/2 = 10.5, which is the required middle value for an even‑length array.
